stories.headline: Google DeepMind AI agents find two weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA; RSA-2048 unaffected

key_facts.fact: On November 6, Google DeepMind said AI agents guided by humans uncovered two major weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems, while modern 2048-bit systems remain safe from these exploits.
key_facts.excerpt: Guided by humans, our models uncovered two major weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems.

key_facts.fact: The work was done with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria; DeepMind found that once an attacker controls roughly half of the signed block or more, padding adds no protection against signature forgery.
key_facts.excerpt: The research, conducted with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria... "Once they control roughly half of the block or more, padding adds no protection at all," Kohli explained.

key_facts.fact: Re-running an earlier academic forgery attack on a 1024-bit key, the agents cut CPU time 3.5-fold, to 391 CPU core-years versus 1,380 in the original study; two agents designed, ran and debugged the computation in under four days with about 20 messages from the human researcher.
key_facts.excerpt: The first forgery took 391 CPU core-years, versus 1,380 in the original study. Two AI agents designed, ran and debugged the forgery computation in under four days, with approximately 20 messages from the human researcher, mostly approvals.

key_facts.fact: For the harder case of a 32-byte hash, DeepMind found an algorithm it estimates is roughly 1,600 times better than the previous best method; this is a theoretical estimate, not an executed computation.
key_facts.excerpt: Even then, DeepMind found an algorithm that by its theoretical estimates is roughly 1,600 times better than the previous best method against 1024-bit keys.

key_facts.fact: A second result, a batch-factoring method called 'fan factories', makes factoring each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper than the best previous batch method after a precomputation costing about one factorization; it has not been implemented.
key_facts.excerpt: a batch factorization method ("fan factories") that, following a precomputation roughly equivalent to the cost of a single factorization, reduces each additional 1024-bit integer to about 1/58 of the cost of a standard number field sieve, which is 30 times less than Coppersmith's MNFS (1993)

key_facts.fact: The algebraic identities in the batch-factoring paper were verified in Lean 4 using two models, one generating proofs and the other verifying them.
key_facts.excerpt: The algebraic identities in the second paper are verified in Lean 4; it was obtained using two models, one generating proofs and the other verifying them.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind said that, in a new era of AI-enabled math, historical hardness assumptions can no longer be relied on and cryptographic standards must be continuously stress-tested.
key_facts.excerpt: As we enter a new era of AI-enabled math and computation, we can no longer rely on historical hardness assumptions and must continuously stress-test cryptographic standards.

stories.headline: Trump says he 'doesn't mind guardrails' on AI as AP reports US safety center drifts to White House

key_facts.fact: In a post-midterm 60 Minutes interview with Ross Douthat aired November 8, Trump said he would work with Democrats on AI safety: 'I don't mind guardrails. But I don't wanna put us in a deep second position. We're leading number one. And China has no guardrails.'
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump: I don't mind guardrails. But I don't wanna put us in a deep second position. We're leading number one. And China has no guardrails, by the way.

key_facts.fact: Trump called himself an 'AI bull', said the risk 'is not nearly as real as they talk' and 'can be managed', and justified the race by saying 'if we don't have it, China's gonna have it.'
key_facts.excerpt: I think that the risk is not nearly as real as it-- as they talk. And I think the risk can be managed.

key_facts.fact: Trump said China is now one year behind the US in AI and that he requires new data centers to build their own power plants.
key_facts.excerpt: China is now one year behind us, which is amazing. ... Every one of those centers that goes up now, under me, is building their own electric.

key_facts.fact: The AP reported on November 8 that officials at CAISSI, the Commerce Department's AI safety evaluation center, were recently asked to informally report to a White House office, citing two former government officials; the center lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing its research.
key_facts.excerpt: the tiny U.S. government division charged with assessing the safety of new AI offerings lacks a permanent leader and has stopped publishing its research. Officials with the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI... recently were asked to informally report to an office of the White House.

key_facts.fact: CAISSI runs on about $10 million a year, roughly one-eighth of its UK counterpart's budget, and had completed more than 40 evaluations through May 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Through May 2026, the center had completed more than 40 evaluations... which operates on an annual budget of $10 million—roughly one-eighth the budget allocated to its counterpart in the United Kingdom.

key_facts.fact: The White House did not answer specific questions about the center and instead pointed to Trump's newly created Super Intelligence Force and a risk study commissioned through the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
key_facts.excerpt: In a statement, the administration pointed to President Donald Trump's creation of a Super Intelligence Force led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton, as well as a risk assessment study commissioned through the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

stories.headline: Gurman: Apple CEO Ternus pushes Federighi to speed AI roadmap; agentic Siri could come in 2027

key_facts.fact: In his Power On newsletter on November 8, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that CEO John Ternus told software chief Craig Federighi in a closed-door meeting that Apple needs to 'accelerate' its software roadmap and 'move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri.'
key_facts.excerpt: Gurman said that Apple CEO John Ternus told Apple's software engineering chief Craig Federighi that Apple needs to "accelerate" its software roadmap and "move quickly beyond merely making necessary improvements to Siri."

key_facts.fact: Gurman said Apple could make Siri work 'more like an agent' as early as next year, comparing it with OpenAI's Dots, Meta's Muse and Grok, which pursue goals without the user initiating every step.
key_facts.excerpt: "Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step," said Gurman. "Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I'm told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year."

key_facts.fact: Ternus is reportedly frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors.
key_facts.excerpt: Ternus, Gurman writes, is frustrated by what he sees as a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors.

key_facts.excerpt: Apple separated the first M1 development milestone into six weeks of coding, exploration, and feature development followed by two weeks of convergence, replacing its customary split of two four-week periods.

stories.headline: Tencent AI chief Yao Shunyu warns AI bio abilities will soon be able to do harm

key_facts.fact: Tencent chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu, a former OpenAI researcher, said at a Hong Kong science symposium on Saturday, November 7: 'The cyber abilities of [AI] models and soon [the] bio ability of models will reach a threshold where it's actually possible to do harm.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The cyber abilities of [AI] models and soon [the] bio ability of models will reach a threshold where it's actually possible to do harm," Yao said at a science symposium co-hosted by the Hong Kong Academy of Sciences and the Future Science Prize.

key_facts.fact: Yao said Chinese companies releasing open models need to take safety very seriously and warned biology risks may be harder to manage than cyber risks.
key_facts.excerpt: He said Chinese companies that release open models, which anyone can download and change, need to take safety very seriously. He also warned that biology risks may be harder to manage than cyber risks.

key_facts.fact: Yao said US firms such as Anthropic make a strong case for keeping top models closed, but argued a mix of open and closed models may work best because open models can also help defenders.
key_facts.excerpt: Yao said US firms such as Anthropic make a strong case for keeping top models closed. However, he argued that a mix of open and closed models may work best, because open models can also help defenders.

key_facts.fact: Tencent launched its flagship Hy4 model on November 4, saying it left exploit material out of training data and that the model is weaker than leading models at designing experiments; it plans to release Hy4's weights and a safety report in the coming days.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent said it left material on exploiting software flaws out of Hy4's training data... Tencent also said that Hy4 has strong basic knowledge of biology, but is weaker than leading models at designing experiments... The company plans to release Hy4's weights and a report on its safety testing in the coming days, Reuters reported.

key_facts.fact: Yao, 29, joined Tencent last year after a year at OpenAI, where he contributed to products including Operator and Deep Research.
key_facts.excerpt: Yao, 29, joined Tencent last year following a one-year stint at OpenAI, where he contributed to products including Operator and Deep Research.

stories.headline: OpenAI's BioBasicsBench tests AI agents on raw wet-lab data; GPT-6 Astra scores 66.7%

key_facts.fact: On November 6, OpenAI introduced BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark built with enzyme-design company Ligo to test whether AI agents can interpret raw experimental data, identify errors and recognize when evidence cannot support a conclusion.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark's 100 tasks test whether agents can interpret raw experimental data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence cannot support a conclusion.

key_facts.fact: At the 'xhigh' reasoning setting, GPT-6 Astra earned 66.7% of available credit versus 43.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol, using 4,704 output tokens per task versus 9,099.
key_facts.excerpt: At the 'xhigh' setting, which allows more reasoning per task, GPT‑6 Astra earned an average of 66.7% of the available credit, compared with 43.8% for GPT‑5.6 Sol.

key_facts.fact: Tasks span five areas: protein methods, imaging and cytometry, quantification and assays, nucleic acid methods and molecular cloning, using gel images, colony plates, microscopy and instrument readouts.
key_facts.excerpt: BioBasicsBench has 100 tasks across five areas of routine wet-lab work: protein methods, imaging and cytometry, quantification and assays, nucleic acid methods, and molecular cloning.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI evaluated seven of its own models across 37 model and reasoning-effort settings, five attempts per task, for 18,500 results; no other lab's models were tested.
key_facts.excerpt: In all, OpenAI ran 37 model-and-setting combinations, with five attempts per task, for 18,500 graded answers. The post compares only OpenAI models.

key_facts.fact: In one task, the top-scoring model read gel bands correctly but reversed the interpretation supported by the controls and recommended colonies still carrying the original plasmid.
key_facts.excerpt: It distinguished the band patterns correctly, then reversed the interpretation supported by the controls and recommended colonies still carrying the original plasmid

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said the benchmark helps track what model gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety and biosecurity.
key_facts.excerpt: BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

stories.headline: Nvidia board opens independent probe as Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy

key_facts.fact: On November 8, 2026, Nvidia's board said it is initiating an independent investigation after reports that founder and CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, overseen by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel.
key_facts.excerpt: The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.

key_facts.fact: The board said it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but will examine all available information, and that it has confidence in Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information... The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team

key_facts.fact: In an email to staff on November 8, Huang wrote that he had been unfaithful to his wife, took full responsibility, said he had fallen short of his responsibility to the board, partners and shareholders, and that he supports the investigation.
key_facts.excerpt: I was unfaithful to my wife... I take full responsibility for what I did... you deserve better from me... I have fallen short of that responsibility... NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.

key_facts.fact: Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which buys Nvidia AI chips and has been scrutinized over suspicions it helped Beijing obtain barred chips, was concluded by US authorities to be a Chinese intelligence asset.
key_facts.excerpt: Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset. US authorities have scrutinized Megaspeed, which buys AI chips from Nvidia, over suspicions it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported on November 8 that Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of a highly classified memo this past spring warning top Trump administration officials about Huang's relationship with the alleged spy.
key_facts.excerpt: Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw the drafting of the highly classified memo this past spring warning top Trump administration officials that Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on November 8 he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations but called him a fine person; China's foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun on November 9 called the spy allegation groundless and a smear.
key_facts.excerpt: "The so-called Chinese spy allegation is groundless," Guo Jiakun, a spokesman for China's foreign ministry told reporters in a regular briefing. "It is nothing but a smear against China."

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell nearly 5% in US premarket trading on November 9; Axios said the stock had already lost 13% since the initial reports through Friday.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia shares were off 4.4% in premarket trading as of 5:15 a.m. ET Monday... Through Friday, the stock had already lost 13% of its value since the initial reports

key_facts.fact: Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia executive, canceled a planned Seoul visit to meet AI chip startup Rebellions and Kakao Mobility; Rebellions cited 'unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.'
key_facts.excerpt: Madison Huang had initially planned to visit South Korean AI startup Rebellions and hold a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said the events were canceled due to "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."

stories.headline: Google adds TPU 8tx for confidential workloads and TPU 8i Max for long-context AI

key_facts.fact: Google is introducing two new variants of its in-house tensor processing units, the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, Bloomberg reported on November 9, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet's Google is introducing two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units, Bloomberg News reported on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Google AI infrastructure chief technologist Amin Vahdat said the variants are not new chips but reconfigured versions; the 8tx targets secure, confidential workloads for government agencies and regulated industries, and the 8i Max targets AI applications that need long context windows.
key_facts.excerpt: The TPU 8tx and 8i Max variants are not new chips, but reconfigured versions designed to handle workloads customers have been asking for... The 8tx is designed for secure and confidential workloads used by government agencies and companies in regulated industries, while the 8i Max is designed for AI applications that require long context windows

key_facts.fact: The 8tx system runs in tandem with AMD chips as part of a partnership between the two companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The system runs in tandem with Advanced Micro Devices' chips as part of a partnership between the two companies. The 8i Max is designed to run AI applications that require long context windows.

key_facts.fact: Google's chip unit used to release one new AI processor every two years; this year it launched two (TPU 8t and 8i), and the new variants expand that lineup to four products.
key_facts.excerpt: The business used to release one new AI processor every two years, but this year it launched two at once... the four TPU products will be optimized for different needs.

key_facts.fact: The two new products are expected to go on sale next year (2027).

stories.headline: Dutch police arrest up to 200 after protesters storm Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam

key_facts.fact: On Friday, November 6, 2026, protesters broke into the construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam, some climbing a crane and setting off flares, in what AP called the latest action in a growing anti-data center movement in Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Protesters broke into a construction site for a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam on Friday, with some climbing a crane and setting off flares while others clashed with police, the latest action in a growing anti-data center movement sweeping Europe.

key_facts.fact: Dutch police said they arrested between 150 and 200 protesters for trespassing; some were found with material suspected stolen from the site and others were suspected of damaging property.
key_facts.excerpt: Dutch police said they arrested between 150 and 200 protesters for trespassing after hundreds entered the construction site of a Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam... material suspected of having been stolen from the site was found on some of those detained

key_facts.fact: Two groups were involved: Fossielvrij, protesting data centers' energy use and gas power, and pro-Palestinian group Geef Tegengas, which opposes Microsoft's services to Israel.
key_facts.excerpt: Fossielvrij betoogde op de bouwlocatie tegen de komst van datacenters, omdat ze veel energie verbruiken en sommige op gas draaien. Een andere groep activisten van het pro-Palestijnse Geef Tegengas was er ook bij. Zij zijn tegen Microsoft omdat het Amerikaanse bedrijf diensten aan Israël levert

key_facts.fact: All of the more than 200 people detained were released by November 7; the data center filed a complaint for trespass, vandalism and burglary.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: ByteDance weighs second phase of Ceará data center, larger than $10B first phase

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is considering expanding its data center project in northeastern Brazil and is seeking a developer to oversee a second phase at an industrial port in Ceará, where it benefits from tax breaks for data exports, Bloomberg reported on November 6, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The Beijing-based company is seeking a developer to oversee the second phase of a project at an industrial port in the state of Ceara, where it benefits from tax breaks for data exports, according to people familiar with the process

key_facts.fact: The new expansion could exceed the $10 billion, 300-megawatt project already under construction at the Port of Pecém.

stories.headline: US opens Task Force Iron Gate on Iran's land routes; Trump calls new strikes 'highly unlikely'

key_facts.fact: US Central Command announced on Saturday, November 7, a new task force, Task Force Iron Gate, to stop Iran from moving advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue across its land borders and the Caspian Sea, extending its naval blockade of Iranian ports.
key_facts.excerpt: Task Force Iron Gate will reinforce "the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea", CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said... preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and illegal revenue streams across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM said a US aircraft disabled the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman, and that since July its blockade had redirected 147 commercial vessels and disabled five merchant ships that refused to comply.
key_facts.excerpt: "Enforcement actions since July have resulted in U.S. forces redirecting 147 commercial vessels that complied", and disabling "five merchant ships that refused to comply"

key_facts.fact: On Sunday, November 8, Trump told CNN that renewed US strikes on Iran were 'highly unlikely' if Tehran signs a strong agreement, while saying three US aircraft carriers in the region were 'locked and loaded' and the US had 38 Iranian bridges it could 'knock down in literally one hour'.
key_facts.excerpt: "It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump said. "The answer is highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."... "We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour."

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X that Iran's two-day proposal stands and that Iran's forces would 'rain down hell' if Washington chooses war; the conflict is now eight months old.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results," Araghchi wrote in a post on X on Sunday. "Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened warriors rain down hell,"

key_facts.fact: IRGC spokesperson Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi said Iran had lifted its self-imposed 2,000-kilometer limit on ballistic missile range after the task force was announced.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohebbi confirmed that Iran was now abandoning its previous 2,000-kilometer, or roughly 1,240-mile, ballistic missile-range restriction... "That restriction has been lifted for us,"

key_facts.fact: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the US Treasury asked Iraq to close all but two of its border crossings with Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Treasury Department asked that Iraq shut down all but two of its border crossings with Iran as part of a drive to isolate Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell about 1.8% toward $96 a barrel on Monday, November 9, after a 16% drop the previous week, as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict continued.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude fell 1.8% toward $96 a barrel, extending last week's 16% drop as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict continued.

stories.headline: US adds 165,000 jobs in October, nearly triple forecasts, lifting odds of a December Fed hike

key_facts.fact: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Friday, November 6, that nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October and the unemployment rate was 4.1%; the 12-month average monthly gain had been 48,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October, higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the prior 12 months.

key_facts.fact: Economists polled by Dow Jones had expected 59,000 jobs; average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% on the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, well above the Wall Street forecast for 59,000... Worker pay rose by 0.4% for a 3.1% annual increase.

key_facts.fact: August and September were revised up by a combined 84,000 jobs, with September moving from 29,000 to 60,000.
key_facts.excerpt: the change for September was revised up by 31,000, from +29,000 to +60,000. With these revisions, employment in August and September combined is 84,000 higher than previously reported.

key_facts.fact: Professional and business services added 70,000 jobs in October, well above its 12-month average gain of 15,000, with professional, scientific and technical services up 33,000.
key_facts.excerpt: Employment in professional and business services increased by 70,000 in October, well above the average monthly gain of 15,000 over the prior 12 months... professional, scientific, and technical services (+33,000)

key_facts.fact: The broader U-6 underemployment rate rose to 7.9% from 7.6%, and the average duration of unemployment rose to 27.1 weeks, the highest since September 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: A more encompassing measure that includes discouraged workers and those holding part-time jobs for economic reasons rose to 7.9%, up 0.3 percentage point... The average duration of unemployment jumped to 27.1 weeks... the highest since September 2021.

key_facts.fact: Market-implied odds of a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December fell to 67% after the post-midterm tech selloff and rose back to 79% after the report.
key_facts.excerpt: The market-implied odds of a December hike dropped to 67% yesterday from 83% on Wednesday... After the release of the jobs report, those odds jumped back up to 79% on Friday.

stories.headline: Europe to join US-led Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi despite Kremlin objections

key_facts.fact: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday, November 8, that European officials would attend the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, after Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had ruled out a European role.
key_facts.excerpt: "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio... The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.

key_facts.fact: An EU official told AFP that national security officials for the EU, NATO, France, Germany and the UK would be on site, though their role is unclear; the Kremlin insists on the Russia-Ukraine-US format.
key_facts.excerpt: An EU official told AFP that national security officials for the bloc, NATO, France, Germany and the UK would be on site -- although how they would be involved is unclear. The Kremlin insisted the talks will still be held in the Russia-Ukraine-US format

key_facts.fact: It will be the first round of trilateral talks since February; Russia's delegation, led by Vladimir Medinsky, will for the first time include deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin and military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky... alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.

key_facts.fact: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Sunday that some progress had been made on Ukraine and Europe's post-war 'security infrastructure', and that this week's talks could advance it further.
key_facts.excerpt: US secretary of state Marco Rubio said some progress had been made on what the "security infrastructure" of Ukraine and Europe could look like after the war with Russia, adding that talks this week could lead to further advances.

key_facts.fact: In a CBS '60 Minutes' interview broadcast November 8, Trump said the war would end soon and that Ukraine would 'end up with a little bit different shape'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I think we're gonna have it done, and I think it's gonna happen and they're gonna end up with a little bit different shape Ukraine," Trump said.

key_facts.fact: US officials say the session will focus on security guarantees to prevent the war from restarting; a ceasefire will not be on the table.
key_facts.excerpt: A cease-fire won't be on the table... negotiators will focus on security guarantees intended to prevent the war from restarting if a cease-fire is reached, U.S. officials have said.

stories.headline: FDA investigates cancer risk from Novartis gene therapy Zolgensma after vector DNA found in tumors

key_facts.fact: The FDA said on November 6 it is investigating a serious risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, in patients treated with Zolgensma, Novartis' AAV gene therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, citing confirmed reports of product-related insertional oncogenesis.
key_facts.excerpt: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has received postmarketing adverse event reports of malignancies in patients treated with Zolgensma... including confirmed reports of product-related insertional oncogenesis involving the GLI1 (Glioma-Associated Oncogene Homolog 1) gene.

key_facts.fact: Three tumor cases involved the GLI1 oncogene; in two, tumor tissue showed Zolgensma's vector DNA integrated into the patient's genome next to or inside GLI1.
key_facts.excerpt: three cases involved tumors associated with the GLI1 oncogene. In two of those cases, molecular analysis of tumor tissue demonstrated Zolgensma AAV vector DNA integration into the host genome

key_facts.fact: The FDA said the risk also applies to Itvisma, the intrathecal version approved in November 2025, because it uses the same vector and construct, though no tumors have been reported with it.
key_facts.excerpt: FDA has determined that the risk of neoplasia, including malignancy, is applicable to both onasemnogene abeparvovec products, Zolgensma... and Itvisma... There have been no reported cases of neoplasia following Itvisma administration to date.

key_facts.fact: The agency said benefits still outweigh risks for approved uses, but it is evaluating whether regulatory action is appropriate and asked that treated patients be monitored for tumors.
key_facts.excerpt: The overall benefits of Zolgensma and Itvisma continue to outweigh their potential risks for their approved uses, though FDA is investigating... and is evaluating whether regulatory action is appropriate.

key_facts.fact: The FDA notice followed Novartis' disclosure a day earlier that nine Zolgensma recipients had developed tumors since the 2019 approval, two with evidence of vector integration.
key_facts.excerpt: Nine people with spinal muscular atrophy who received Novartis' gene therapy Zolgensma later developed tumors, and two cases displayed evidence that the virus used to deliver the treatment fused itself into patient DNA

key_facts.fact: The FDA also pointed to two published reports of AAV integration-driven tumors in other gene therapy programs, FBX-101 and RGX-111, and said it is monitoring similar AAV therapies.
key_facts.excerpt: FDA is aware of two published reports of AAV vector integration-driven oncogenesis in other programs: a GLI1 integration event in the FBX-101 program... and a PLAG1 integration event in the RGX-111 program

stories.headline: NASA picks eight firms for $10B Moon lander contract and greenlights nuclear PROMISE rover

key_facts.fact: NASA on Saturday, November 7, selected eight companies for CLPS 2, a 10-year lunar delivery contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion: Blue Origin, Firefly Aerospace, Intuitive Machines, ispace-U.S., Lockheed Martin Space, Northrop Grumman Space Systems, SpaceX and Voyager Technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA selected eight companies for the next phase of its CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative... a 10-year, multiple-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity master contract with a combined maximum value of $10 billion.

key_facts.fact: The $10 billion is a ceiling for future task orders, not money already awarded; NASA also raised the original CLPS contract from $2.6 billion to $4.2 billion for the first phase of its Moon Base.
key_facts.excerpt: The new Commercial Lunar Payload Services framework has a maximum combined value of $10 billion over 10 years, with the figure representing a ceiling for future task orders, not money already awarded

key_facts.fact: NASA is moving ahead with PROMISE, a six-wheeled nuclear-powered rover built by JPL from spare Curiosity and Perseverance hardware, to drill about 1 meter into the lunar South Pole surface for ice; launch is targeted for late 2028 with an 18-month mission.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory... will manage the mission and build the rover from a combination of spare flight components and engineering test models for NASA's Curiosity and Perseverance Mars rovers... NASA is targeting late 2028 to launch PROMISE and planning an 18-month mission

key_facts.fact: Blue Origin won a $94 million base contract, with a $140 million performance option, to land PROMISE on its Mark 1 lander.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA awarded Blue Origin a $94 million base contract, with an option period worth an additional $140 million based on performance to deliver PROMISE to the lunar South Pole.

key_facts.fact: NASA expects PROMISE to cost under $400 million including instruments and launch; CLPS 2 is designed for landers carrying two to six metric tons.
key_facts.excerpt: CLPS 2 is built for Phase 2 landers carrying two to six metric tons... NASA expects to cost under $400 million including instruments and the ride to the Moon.

key_facts.fact: About $1.3 billion in launch and orbital transfer flights went to Arrow Science, Blue Origin and Impulse Space as part of the same package.

stories.headline: Crédit Agricole proposes merging its Italian unit with Banco BPM to form Italy's No. 3 bank

key_facts.fact: Crédit Agricole on Monday, November 9, proposed talks to merge Crédit Agricole Italia with Banco BPM, creating Italy's third-largest banking group with 6.5 million customers and more than 2,300 branches.
key_facts.excerpt: This strategic project would create Italy's third-largest banking group, serving 6.5 million customers through more than 2,300 branches

key_facts.fact: The offer includes an exchange ratio reflecting a 20% premium plus a €1 billion extraordinary dividend to Banco BPM shareholders, with expected synergies of €800 million a year.
key_facts.excerpt: the proposal provides for an exchange ratio that reflects a 20% premium, in addition to the payment of an extraordinary dividend of Euro 1 billion to Banco BPM's current shareholders. The expected synergies are estimated at Euro 800 million per year.

key_facts.fact: Crédit Agricole's stake would rise from 29.6% to about 45% of the combined bank, which would stay listed in Milan, without a mandatory takeover bid if Banco BPM shareholders approve a 'whitewash' exemption.
key_facts.excerpt: a deal that would lift its stake in the Milan-listed lender to about 45% from 29.6% without a mandatory takeover offer

key_facts.fact: Banco BPM CEO Giuseppe Castagna would lead the combined entity, and the deal could close in the second half of 2027, subject to ECB and Italian 'golden power' approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal could be finalised in the second half of 2027. Giuseppe Castagna 'would be confirmed as chief executive of the new entity'.

key_facts.fact: Banco BPM shares rose more than 9% in early trading after the announcement.
key_facts.excerpt: Banco BPM's share price was up by over 9% in early trading on Monday following Crédit Agricole's announcement.

key_facts.fact: The proposal comes after Monte dei Paschi shareholders rejected a defensive merger with BPM last month, leaving Intesa Sanpaolo's takeover of MPS set to go ahead.
key_facts.excerpt: Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) CEO Luigi Lovaglio had proposed a merger with BPM as part of his strategy to fend off a takeover bid by Italy's biggest bank, Intesa Sanpaolo, but MPS shareholders rejected the defensive plan last month and that takeover now looks set to go ahead.

stories.headline: OCC gives Coinbase final approval for a federally chartered national trust bank

key_facts.fact: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approved the charter for Coinbase National Trust Company on Friday, November 6, the company announced on Monday, November 9.
key_facts.excerpt: Last Friday, the OCC approved our application to charter Coinbase National Trust Company. This is an important next chapter for Coinbase and for the trusted custody services we have built for more than a decade.

key_facts.fact: The final approval follows a preliminary conditional approval in April 2026; the trust bank offers federally regulated custody and payments but does not take deposits or make loans.
key_facts.excerpt: The Coinbase National Trust had received its provisional approval in April, allowing the company to offer federally regulated custodial and payments services, though not acting as a full-service bank that would take deposits and extend loans.

key_facts.fact: The uninsured national trust bank must hold at least $60 million in tier 1 capital, and Coinbase's entire custody business will migrate to it over a three-year period.
key_facts.excerpt: approving a noninsured national trust bank with a requirement to maintain at least $60 million in tier 1 capital... The entire custody business is to migrate from Coinbase Custody Trust Company to the national trust bank over the three-year de novo period.

key_facts.fact: Coinbase says its immediate focus is digital-asset custody, with plans to move later into stablecoin issuance, white-label stablecoins for other companies and payments.
key_facts.excerpt: Coinbase says its immediate focus following the final approval is to conduct custody of digital assets and eventually move into stablecoin issuance, servicing, offering white-label stablecoin arrangements for other companies and payments.

key_facts.fact: Ripple has already reached the same full national trust bank status, and many other crypto firms hold provisional charters as the OCC implements the GENIUS Act on stablecoins.
key_facts.excerpt: Ripple also achieved that status, and many other firms are obtaining provisional trust charters as the OCC has implemented the GENIUS Act that governs how such trusts can be involved in issuing stablecoins.
